title: Serological and transcriptomic response of African fruit bats to immune challenge with recombinant vaccines expressing Ebola or Nipah virus antigens

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the knowledge gap regarding antibody production and gene expression in bats following exposure to vaccines encoding Nipah virus or Ebola virus antigens. Bats are hosts to diverse zoonotic viruses which can cause high case fatality rates in humans.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved measuring antibody production and gene expression in two African bat species, Eidolon helvum (confirmed reservoir of henipaviruses) and Epomophorus gambianus (putative reservoir of filoviruses), following injection with vaccines expressing either a Nipah virus G glycoprotein or an Ebola virus GP glycoprotein.
analysis.methods: Using a Luminex-based multiplex microsphere immunoassay and a pseudotype virus neutralization assay, the researchers observed an increase in antibodies against the Nipah glycoprotein in most bats that received the Nipah vaccine. Transcriptomic analysis in Eidolon helvum revealed differential gene expression in response to the Ebola vaccine.
analysis.main_results: The study observed an increase in antibodies against the Nipah glycoprotein in most bats that received the Nipah vaccine. In contrast, anti-Ebola glycoprotein antibodies were only detected in Epomophorus gambianus in response to the Ebola vaccine. Transcriptomic analysis in Eidolon helvum showed that genes involved in ISGylation and T-cell differentiation pathways were differentially expressed in response to the Ebola vaccine.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrate species-specific differences in responses to antigen exposure, offering insights into bat adaptive immune systems and providing calibration for serological data from wild bats.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide valuable insights into the adaptive immune systems of bats and offer a framework for calibrating serological data from wild bat populations, which can inform surveillance and diagnostic strategies for Nipah virus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on two specific bat species and the use of vaccines rather than actual viral exposure, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the serological and transcriptomic responses of two African bat species, Eidolon helvum and Epomophorus gambianus, to vaccines expressing Nipah virus or Ebola virus antigens. The research aimed to address the knowledge gap regarding immune responses in bats to these viruses, as detecting them in wild populations is challenging. Using a Luminex-based multiplex microsphere immunoassay and pseudotype virus neutralization assay, the study found that most Eidolon helvum bats developed antibodies against the Nipah glycoprotein after receiving the Nipah vaccine, while only one species, Epomophorus gambianus, showed a response to the Ebola vaccine. Transcriptomic analysis in Eidolon helvum revealed differential expression of genes involved in ISGylation and T-cell differentiation pathways in response to the Ebola vaccine. These results highlight species-specific immune responses to antigen exposure, offering insights into bat immune systems and potential calibration for serological data from wild bats. The study's findings have implications for understanding zoonotic virus transmission and improving surveillance and diagnostic strategies for Nipah virus. However, the study is limited by its focus on vaccinated bats rather than natural viral exposure and the use of only two species, which may affect generalizability.

title: CRISPR/Cas13a-Based Nucleic Acid-Functionalized Discrete Floating-Gate Field-Effect Transistor for Amplification-Free Rapid Nipah Virus Detection

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly lethal zoonotic pathogen, and existing rapid diagnostic tools are scarce and reliant on nucleic acid amplification.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In this study, we designed and fabricated a thin-film field-effect transistor with an IGZO channel and, for the first time, combined a discrete AuNP floating gate with the CRISPR/Cas13a system to achieve amplification-free detection of NiV.
analysis.methods: A pair of partially complementary nucleic acid reporter probes was used to attach AuNPs onto the channel, forming a nucleic acid-functionalized discrete floating gate.
analysis.main_results: Under positive gate voltage, the AuNPs electrostatically induce mirror charges in the IGZO channel, amplifying the sensing signal.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This study not only provides a reliable and rapid detection tool for NiV but also establishes a biosensing framework applicable to other pathogens.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The AuNPs are immobilized via nucleic acid strands, ensuring good biocompatibility.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: CrRNA was designed and the CRISPR system was optimized for compatibility with the FET, achieving amplification-free detection of NiV standards down to 10° copies/μL within 10 min.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a novel CRISPR/Cas13a-based biosensing platform for rapid, amplification-free detection of Nipah virus (NiV). The platform utilizes a thin-film field-effect transistor (FET) with an IGZO channel and a discrete AuNP floating gate functionalized with nucleic acid reporter probes. The design leverages electrostatic induction of mirror charges under positive gate voltage and Fowler–Nordheim tunneling under negative gate voltage to enhance sensitivity. The system was optimized to detect NiV standards at concentrations as low as 10° copies/μL within 10 minutes, demonstrating high specificity and biocompatibility. The findings establish a versatile biosensing framework that could be adapted for other pathogens, offering significant potential for improving diagnostic capabilities in public health settings. The study's results are supported by target-specific methods and are limited by the absence of direct clinical validation.

title: Absence of Nipah virus antibodies and detection of Porcine kobuvirus, Porcine enterovirus-9 and Bocavirus in pigs during a Nipah virus outbreak investigation in West Bengal, India

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of local pig populations in Nipah virus transmission during an outbreak in West Bengal, India, and to screen for other potential etiologies. The Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly lethal zoonotic virus that causes respiratory disease and encephalitis in humans.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in West Bengal during the NiV outbreak in January 2026, focusing on 119 domestic pigs from Nadia, Kolkata, North 24 Paraganas, and Purba Bardhaman districts. The investigation sought to determine if pigs were involved in NiV transmission and to screen for other viruses.
analysis.methods: Virological and serological tests for NiV infection were performed using real-time qRT-PCR and swine IgG ELISA. A subset of nasal and rectal swab samples from diseased pigs also underwent metagenomic sequencing to detect other viruses.
analysis.main_results: All swab samples tested negative for NiV RNA, and no antibodies were found in the serum samples. Metagenomic sequencing detected genomes of Porcine Kobuvirus (PKV) and Porcine enterovirus 9 (PEV9), prevalent in the Indian pig population, as well as Porcine Bocavirus (PBoV), which is relatively infrequently reported from India.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that pigs were not involved in NiV transmission during the outbreak and highlight the presence of other porcine viruses in the region. This adds to the limited molecular reports of PBoV from India.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results emphasize the importance of genomic surveillance and the integration of the One Health concept into disease monitoring, particularly for emerging pathogens like Nipah virus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to a single outbreak investigation and did not include long-term monitoring or broader ecological data. The evidence for NiV absence is strong, but the detection of other viruses may not fully address the transmission dynamics of Nipah virus.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the role of domestic pigs in Nipah virus (NiV) transmission during an outbreak in West Bengal, India, in January 2026. It collected blood, nasal, rectal, throat, and ocular swab samples from 119 pigs and tested them for NiV using real-time qRT-PCR and swine IgG ELISA. All samples tested negative for NiV RNA, and no antibodies were detected in serum samples. Metagenomic sequencing identified Porcine Kobuvirus (PKV), Porcine enterovirus 9 (PEV9), and Porcine Bocavirus (PBoV) in the pigs, contributing to limited molecular reports of PBoV in India. The authors concluded that pigs were not involved in NiV transmission during the outbreak and emphasized the need for genomic surveillance and the One Health approach in disease monitoring. The study's findings are strong for NiV absence but limited in scope, as they focus on a single outbreak and do not provide broader ecological insights.

title: Serological and transcriptomic response of African fruit bats to immune challenge with recombinant vaccines expressing Ebola or Nipah virus antigens

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the serological and transcriptomic immune responses of African fruit bats to immune challenge with recombinant vaccines expressing Ebola or Nipah virus antigens, addressing the lack of in vivo immunological studies on bat antibodies against zoonotic viruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in experimental facilities in Ghana with 19 African straw-coloured fruit bats (Ei. gambianus) captured from their roosts in Accra, and samples were collected over two months with individuals placed in single-species groups of up to five bats.
analysis.methods: Antibody responses to Nipah and Ebola antigens were measured using a Luminex-based multiplex microsphere immunoassay, and transcriptomic data were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes and pathways in response to the vaccines.
analysis.main_results: The Nipah vaccine group showed a significant increase in anti-Nipah-G antibody binding compared to the PBS group (Wilcoxon rank-sum test: W = 76, p = 0.0026), with MFI values comparable to those of a monoclonal antibody. A linear mixed-effects model confirmed the significant effect of the Nipah vaccine on antibody levels (p < 10−4).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The observed antibody kinetics provide insights into the in vivo immune response to Nipah virus antigens in bats, highlighting the potential of serological markers for surveillance of zoonotic pathogens, though they do not confirm viral exposure or production kinetics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings contribute to understanding the immune responses of bats to Nipah virus antigens, which is critical for improving surveillance strategies and developing vaccines against zoonotic pathogens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by the use of a small sample size and the challenges of maintaining containment level 4 facilities, but the evidence is moderate due to the controlled experimental setting and statistical validation of results.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the serological and transcriptomic immune responses of African fruit bats to recombinant vaccines expressing Nipah or Ebola virus antigens. Bats were captured in Ghana and housed in controlled environments for two months. Antibody responses were measured using a Luminex-based assay, and transcriptomic data were analyzed to identify gene expression changes. The Nipah vaccine group showed a significant increase in anti-Nipah-G antibody binding compared to the PBS control group, with MFI values comparable to monoclonal antibody levels. title: Immunomodulatory RIG-I Agonist SLR14 Confers Protection Against a Range of Highly Pathogenic Negative Sense RNA viruses

analysis.research_question_and_background: Emerging and re-emerging zoonotic RNA viruses, including filoviruses, henipaviruses and Rift Valley Fever virus (RVFV), pose a significant threat to human health. Due to their epidemic potential and high pathogenicity, these viruses are categorized as WHO priority pathogens, yet we still lack effective medical countermeasures (MCMs) against most of these dangerous pathogens, supporting that host-directed antivirals will be advantageous for broadly acting MCMs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here we assessed the antiviral efficacy of SLR14, an immunomodulatory stem-loop RNA that activates RIG-I, for its activity against a panel of highly pathogenic viruses.
analysis.methods: SLR14 treatment provided broad-spectrum protection, markedly reducing infection with Ebola virus (EBOV), Marburg virus, and Sudan virus in human primary monocyte-derived macrophages, and Nipah virus replication in iPSC-derived endothelial cells, whether administered prophylactically or therapeutically.
analysis.main_results: In vivo, a single dose of SLR14 protected mice against lethal RVFV infection when administered prophylactically, and, notably, retained significant efficacy when administered up to two days post-infection. Therapeutic SLR14 administration also improved survival rates of EBOV-infected mice.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Although EBOV infection and SLR14 treatment activated overlapping innate immune pathways in human macrophages, viral infection induced a nonprotective response, whereas SLR14 elicited a well-regulated, markedly stronger and protective interferon-stimulated and inflammatory gene signature while avoiding prolonged IFN gene upregulation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Our data identify SLR14 as a potent host-directed therapeutic with broad antiviral efficacy against some of the most lethal viral pathogens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: However, the study does not report on the long-term effects of SLR14 treatment and the generalizability of the findings to other host species remains to be determined.

analysis.summary_en: The study evaluated the antiviral efficacy of SLR14, an RIG-I agonist, against a range of highly pathogenic viruses, including Ebola, Marburg, and Nipah viruses. SLR14 provided broad-spectrum protection, reducing viral replication and improving survival rates in both in vitro and in vivo models. The findings suggest SLR14 as a potent host-directed therapeutic with potential for use against lethal viral pathogens.

title: Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on Nipah virus (Henipavirus nipahense), Nipah virus infection and disease. The central question is the development of broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals (BSAs) against RNA viruses, including Nipah virus, with activity spanning multiple genera, entire families, or even crossing viral families.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic overview of approved and investigational antiviral agents active against RNA viruses, including Nipah virus. It discusses the rationale for developing BSAs and outlines the biological determinants underlying their antiviral spectrum. The review does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates but provides a non-exhaustive overview of existing and experimental drugs.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the development of broader-acting small molecule antivirals is essential to address current unmet medical needs and to strengthen epidemic and pandemic preparedness. title: Epitope and immunological basis for superior immunogenicity of henipavirus glycoprotein HeV.G over NiV.G in mRNA vaccines

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nipah (NiV) and Hendra (HeV) viruses are highly lethal zoonotic Henipaviruses with pandemic potential, for which no licensed vaccines exist. The surface glycoprotein (G) is the primary target of neutralizing antibodies, yet a systematic comparison of the immunogenicity of NiV.G and HeV.G has been lacking.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we engineered mRNA vaccines encoding the full-length G proteins of NiV and HeV. In Syrian hamsters, while both vaccines conferred homologous protection, only HeV.G vaccination at a lower dose (5 μg) provided complete cross-protection against lethal NiV challenge.
analysis.methods: Comparative immune profiling revealed that HeV.G vaccination induced significantly higher neutralizing antibody titers, which correlated with robust germinal center B cell expansion and a stronger CD4 + T follicular helper (Tfh) cell response, despite equivalent B cell activation.
analysis.main_results: Epitope mapping uncovered a structurally conserved yet immunologically divergent MHC class II-restricted peptide (YIAITKVER) in HeV.G with superior predicted binding affinity, providing a mechanistic basis for the enhanced T cell help.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our work establishes HeV.G as a superior vaccine immunogen due to its distinct epitope repertoire and underscores the critical role of CD4 + T cell help in driving cross-protective B cell immunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Collectively, this study defines HeV.G as the preferred antigen for pan-henipavirus vaccine development and offers a framework for rational antigen selection against future viral threats.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength for the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the immunogenicity of the glycoprotein (G) from Nipah virus (NiV) and Hendra virus (HeV) in mRNA vaccines. It highlights the lack of systematic comparison between NiV.G and HeV.G, despite their shared status as highly lethal zoonotic Henipaviruses. The research engineered mRNA vaccines encoding the full-length G proteins of both viruses and evaluated their protective efficacy in Syrian hamsters. Results showed that HeV.G vaccination at a lower dose (5 μg) provided complete cross-protection against lethal NiV challenge, while both vaccines offered homologous protection. Immune profiling revealed that HeV.G induced significantly higher neutralizing antibody titers, associated with robust B cell expansion and a stronger CD4+ T follicular helper (Tfh) cell response, despite equivalent B cell activation. Epitope mapping identified a structurally conserved yet immunologically divergent MHC class II-restricted peptide in HeV.G with superior predicted binding affinity, explaining the enhanced T cell help. The study concludes that HeV.G is a superior vaccine immunogen for pan-henipavirus development, emphasizing the role of CD4+ T cell help in cross-protective immunity. It also suggests the potential of multivalent vaccines in broadening immune coverage. The findings do not report specific limitations, but the evidence is strong due to the direct comparison of immunogenicity and mechanistic insights.
